As part of this concept study, several potential manufacturers were engaged for high level / budgetary supply quotations. 1. Idesa: Located in Asturias, Spain, Idesa has provided a proposal for 11 off horizontal pressure vessels. This option is the basis of our design, providing for the preferred layout and improved constructability. This manufacturer is familiar to Entr / Aker Solutions having delivered Liquid CO 2 storage units previously. 2. Chart Industries: Located in Theodore, Alabama, USA, has provided a proposal for 17 horizontal pressure vessels. 17 tanks were necessary to reach the total desired hub storage capacity of 30,000 m3 due to size limitations at Chart’s manufacturing facility, whereas Idesa can provide a Page57 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version smaller number of larger tanks. This option has been screened out of this phase of the study as the increased number of units was not ideal from construction, layout, and operation aspects. This option will be reevaluated during future design phases. 3. American Tank and Vessel: This company is very interested in the project and has ample experience building and delivering large, specialized tanks throughout two dozen countries. They have several manufacturing facilities in the southern U.S. and proposed building spherical tanks onsite rather than transporting spheres or bullet tanks from their manufacturing base. However, they have no experience with liquified CO and their engineering and materials selection needs 2 further study. 4. Trans Tech Energy: Unable to manufacture vessels to project requirements. 5. OEG Cryogenics: Unable to manufacture vessels to project requirements 6. RFCC: Located in Heibei Province, China. Maximum size vessel RFCC can manufacture is 500 m3, resulting in over 60 pressure vessels being required to satisfy the T-RICH storage volume requirement. In the next phase of the project, it is essential to engage in detailed discussions with various pump vendors to identify the optimal pump type and design that are suited for the purpose with a low NPSHR to prevent Page58 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version pump cavitation. It is also recommended that the plant receives subcooled LCO delivered by rail cars 2 and trucks. Critical service centrifugal pumps shall be designed, manufactured, inspected, and tested in accordance with API 610, the equipment and ancillaries shall comply with the normative references listed within API 610. Centrifugal pumps in non-critical service pumps shall be designed, manufactured, inspected, and tested in accordance with ISO5199.
